newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Opposition leads Romania parliamentary poll.
newsitem.headline: Opposition leads Romania parliamentary poll.

text.p: Romania's centrist opposition has a strong lead over its ex-communist foes in parliamentary elections, first official results showed on Monday.
The Democratic Convention (CDR), which pledges swift reform to tackle widespread poverty in Romania, now looks strong enough to lead a coalition to end seven years of government by former communists.
But in the presidential race the incumbent Ion Iliescu has edged ahead, doing better than exit polls predicted.
In the presidential contest, due to go to a second round in two weeks time, Iliescu won 31.8 percent support to CDR leader Emil Constantinescu's 28.5 percent.

With around a fifth of the votes counted official figures from the Central Election Bureau put former prime minister Petre Roman in third place with 21.4 percent. His votes will play a pivotal role in the run-off.
But the CDR was well out in front in races for both houses of parliament.
In the lower Chamber of Deputies, it had 30.8 percent, compared to 20.8 percent for Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy. Figures for the upper house, the Senate, were broadly similar.
Roman's Social Democratic Union (USD) was third with 13 percent in both chambers and looks set to hold the balance of power in any coalition government.
Both the CDR and USD have refused to cut any coalition deal with Iliescu's PDSR, which they say is corrupt and inept in dealing with Romania's protracted economic crisis.
But personal rivalry between the two opposition leaders blocked conclusion of any formal post-election pact.
Iliescu appealed to the CDR after exit polls were announced to consider aligning itself with his ruling party.
The ethnic Hungarian UDMR party, generally unfriendly to Iliescu, also held a pivotal position in fourth place with some six percent.
Romanian nationalist parties look to be the only other political groups scoring strongly enough to beat the three percent threshold for a place in parliament.
